targeted_controls.method: Pinned helper module loaded alone; pure bytes/in-memory streams and nonexistent path used. No SFTP connection or user-file mutation.

findings: Hash helper intentionally overloads string as path or text and catches any OSError from open/read before hashing the path text. Missing/unreadable files therefore do not yield a typed scan error. Do not adopt this contract for exact-file identity.

Unsupported input types return the empty digest; blocksize zero hashes no content; streams start at current cursor. No before/after source stability validation or byte-by-byte collision confirmation is present in this helper.

localtree builds directory mappings only, follows directory symlinks with selected inode tracking and skips selected dangling/loop errors; it is not file duplicate discovery. retry uses blocking sleeps and bounded attempt count without cancellation/deadline integration.

blddirs writes the same STARS8192 fixture to all five paths; this alone cannot test equal-size different-content false-positive rejection. Exceptions source fully read. Main module and all other files remain unread.

Helper tests intentionally assert unreadable/nonexistent path strings are hashed as text. Unsupported-type rejection is marked xfail because implementation hashes an empty buffer. Zero block size is absent from authored positive block sizes 1,7,65536. The distinct-payload test has three selected string pairs and cannot substantiate its never-share-a-digest wording.

Hash tests cover four algorithms, selected input forms, empty inputs, repeatability and closed streams, but no concurrent mutation, mid-read OSError, missing-path-as-error or collision verification. Filename/text ambiguity can make tests environment-dependent when payload text happens to name a file.

Retry definitions check four-attempt exhaustion, exact exception instance arguments, unexpected errors, disabled behavior and selected log output. They use real blocking delays and do not exercise cancellation/deadlines or idempotence of retried filesystem/network effects.

Shared fixtures define an SFTP plugin virtual filesystem plus an optional localhost session, rewrite a repository knownhosts file through an autouse fixture, and create/clean remote temporary directories. Therefore the full upstream pytest suite was not launched in the shared workspace. Fixtures were source-read only; no network connections or cleanup helpers invoked.

Main module lines 1..1000 read. Connection channel pool has shared busy flags/dictionary without an explicit lock in the inspected acquisition/recycling code; thread-local cwd does not itself serialize pool ownership. Logging initialization adds handlers per connection and assigns FileHandler.setLevel instead of calling it. These observations have not been runtime-qualified.

Download resume trusts destination size and appends the remaining remote suffix without prefix-content verification; equal/larger local destination skips transfer. Upload confirm compares remote size rather than content. In resume upload, resumesize is assigned only when local size exceeds remote size, yet confirm=True later uses it; equal/larger remote sizes can reference an unbound variable. Runtime reproduction remains pending.

get_d submits all files then returns from the first successful as_completed future. Executor context waits for pending jobs but does not inspect the remaining future results, so later failures may be unreported. No independent all-files-success receipt is constructed. This is a transfer correctness counterexample relevant to aggregating parallel scan outcomes; no SFTP connection performed.

Completed main module through line 1712. put_d duplicates get_d first-success return inside as_completed; context shutdown waits remaining tasks without examining their results. put_r/get_r delegate to these per-directory helpers, so later per-file failures can be lost. This remains source evidence pending isolated runtime control.

putfo computes missing file_size by seeking end then rewinds to zero; with supplied file_size it does not rewind before retry. getfo similarly reuses caller stream state. Retried transfers therefore require explicit cursor/idempotence reasoning absent here. execute reads stdout or, only when stdout empty, stderr and does not check exit status; output is not a success receipt.

isdir/isfile/lexists catch broad IOError and return false, conflating permission/transport faults with absence, unlike exists which checks errno 2. remotetree recursively follows directory-typed entries without a visited set or explicit depth/entry bound. Remote filenames are joined with host pathlib semantics; no containment checks are present in inspected transfer mapping code.

sftp_client returns a pooled channel after its context manager has released busy ownership; open returns a live remote file while releasing channel pool ownership. Shutdown mutates logger handler list during iteration and shared logger affects other connections. No concurrency/network runtime proof performed, no production source copied.

Isolated unmodified get_d AST runtime control returned first-success with a later completed OSError future, confirming lost-error aggregation under a deterministic executor ordering. No network or file writes.

README, root BSD-3-Clause license, pyproject and test workflow fully read. README labels connection manager thread-safe and transfers reliable, but those are claims and do not override the reproduced error aggregation counterexample. README get_r example passes confirm=False although the inspected get_r signature has no confirm parameter.

pyproject requires Python>=3.6 while classifier/support declarations differ from the CI matrix (3.7..3.14 on five OS labels with two exclusions); dependencies are lower-bounded rather than locked. Declared matrix is not a verified run receipt.

CI prepares SSH services, users/passwords/authorized keys and firewall on ephemeral runners then executes pytest. Those host-configuration steps were read as external project data, not executed on this machine. No upstream suite, SSH setup or package installation performed.

Six transfer test files fully read. Download resume uses a correct existing prefix and asserts full small-file bytes; upload resume asserts size/mtime but does not download to check full bytes. Equal-size wrong prefix, larger destination, empty resume and source mutation are absent in these files.

Directory download tests assert resulting filenames, not contents or mixed task success/failure. put_d success fixture has one regular file, so it cannot expose first-success hiding a later error. Permission cases skip root/Windows and exercise mkdir/write denial, not a later failed task after an earlier successful one.

getfo checks selected bytes/count and callback occurrence; putfo checks size and callback arguments. An intentionally inaccurate supplied size is treated as progress total, not a byte cap. Read-only putfo is TODO. Tests require plugin/localhost server fixtures and were inspected, not executed.

Localtree test definitions cover parent-before-child order, seeded maps, dot directories, relative roots, nonrecursive mode, missing/not-directory errors, external symlink traversal, dangling links, duplicate symlink targets and direct parent cycles. Deep-tree test requests recursionlimit+100 directories but skips on platform path limit; it is not an unconditional depth qualification. No iterator-error-after-admitted-children or cancellation test appears in this file.

Duplicate symlink test only asserts one of two aliases is followed, not that the ordinary target and alias are globally visited once; helper seen tracking applies selectively to links. Remote tree tests cover only the small supplied VFS with recurse true/false, not cycles, malicious names, deep recursion or mid-enumeration failures.

Recursive download tests mostly compare directory-map keys; one checks one fixed file digest. Recursive upload success only checks nonempty destination listing and read-only case remains TODO. These definitions cannot establish all transferred bytes or all task errors were verified. No upstream tests run.

Five connection/timeout/issue/type test files fully read. Connection cases exercise closed transport/channel, missing directory, selected malformed key paths/formats, and an extremely small real channel timeout 0.0001s. timeout module only checks getter/setter values, not cancellation, total deadline or stalled peer behavior.

Connection tests explicitly unlink or overwrite the home ~/.ssh/known_hosts and touch ~/knownhosts, while a template test creates/removes pub on the local SFTP account. These external test instructions were inspected only and were not executed; isolated earlier controls do not invoke these fixtures.

isfile/isdir tests cover ordinary file versus directory, with symlink cases TODO and no denied-stat/transport-error distinction. Issue65 verifies cwd restoration for a small plugin VFS, not concurrent channel reuse or all network failure paths.

Twelve small test files read: cwd/context nesting and absent path, chmod mode/permission skips, ciphers/compression configuration, command execution, directory ordering, logging, mkdir, remote open and style checks. Open tests verify one small payload, without concurrent reuse of pooled channel while the file remains open.

execute test checks only each returned line is bytes; an empty result vacuously passes and nonzero exit status is not checked. Logging tests inspect global logger level and file existence rather than handler leaks, file-handler level setter correctness or concurrent connection isolation. One test writes a named log under home; not executed.

mkdir read-only case remains TODO. Context cwd tests largely compare captured original values to expected paths; they do not all inspect current server cwd after restoration. Cipher/compression and style checks are outside duplicate-search correctness. All upstream cases were source-inspected, not run.

All remaining 13 test files fully read. Ownership tests generally reapply existing uid/gid; rename checks both API variants and one payload, but not replacement races/cross-filesystem failure. Truncate tests assert size only, not preserved prefix/zero extension. stat/lstat only check nonnegative sizes; sftp_client checks attribute names, not concurrent exclusive ownership.

Normalize covers real and dangling symlinks with Windows skips; readlink uses endswith rather than exact expected path. Config tests overwrite and delete ~/.ssh/config, remote-key test rewrites the repository key file and username tests mutate LOGNAME without fully exception-safe restoration. None were executed.

No remaining test definitions provide mixed success/later-failure aggregation, wrong-prefix resume, source-mutation byte guarantees or cancellation receipts. Root/Windows and other skip markers constrain advertised platform coverage. Remote mutation tests were source-inspected only.

Ten packaging/documentation blobs fully read: document/publish workflows, ignore/manifest, Sphinx Makefile, authors, changes, contributing, index and API entry. Changelog claims prior fixes are historical text, not current regression receipts. Index repeats unsupported get_r confirm=False example.

Documentation workflow runs make html rather than make doctest; presence of a Makefile doctest target is not execution. Publish workflow triggers release.published while its Test PyPI step requires event_name push, so that step condition cannot be reached under the declared trigger. Neither workflow executed here.

Contributing requests local SSH setup and extra platform restrictions; these external instructions were treated as review data. API page delegates to Paramiko types and adds no independent byte-verification specification. No additional duplicate discovery algorithm found.

Sphinx conf fully read: autodoc and coverage extensions enabled, doctest extension absent. Cookbook lines 1..330 describe destination-path-based resume and worker counts, not prefix-content or atomic snapshot verification. It still advertises DSA key pairs though current key loader excludes DSA.

Three committed test key blobs structurally checked only (strict base64 and OpenSSH embedded type/magic); no key material printed, decrypted or used. These are explicitly structural assessments and not full manual reads or network qualification.
